prompt: Build a Customer Portal, Create GitHub Repo, Deploy to Azure and if deployment fails find root cause and solve it.

task.t: Recursively decompose modules into executable tasks
task.d: Derived from the real planning execution.

ro.w: Derived from one real OpenAI planning execution.

analysis.objective: Build a secure customer-facing web portal, maintain its source code in a GitHub repository, and deploy it to Microsoft Azure.
assumptions: The portal will initially support customer authentication, profile management, a dashboard, and support requests.
A responsive web application with an API and relational database is appropriate.
Azure and GitHub credentials, subscription access, domain details, and branding assets will be supplied before deployment.
Infrastructure and deployments should be reproducible through infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD.

proposedStack.backend: Next.js server APIs or a separate Node.js TypeScript API if scaling boundaries require it
proposedStack.authentication: Microsoft Entra External ID or Azure AD B2C, subject to tenant availability
proposedStack.monitoring: Azure Application Insights and Log Analytics

functionalScope: Customer registration, sign-in, sign-out, and password recovery
Support request creation and status tracking
Role-based access for customers and administrators
nonFunctionalRequirements: No secrets committed to source control
Input validation and secure authorization checks
Centralized logs, metrics, health checks, and alerts
requiredInputs: GitHub organization or account and repository visibility
Azure tenant, subscription, region, and resource naming constraints
Expected customer volume and availability target
Required portal features and external integrations
successCriteria: The application passes linting, type checks, automated tests, and security checks.
The GitHub repository contains application code, infrastructure code, workflows, and operational documentation.
The Azure environment can be provisioned reproducibly.
A deployment workflow can release the application without exposing credentials.
Health checks, telemetry, alerts, rollback, and troubleshooting procedures are available.
Deployment failures are diagnosed from evidence, corrected through code or configuration, and verified by rerunning relevant checks.

actions: Confirm users, workflows, integrations, compliance constraints, service-level objectives, and environments.
Define the data model, authorization matrix, API contracts, and threat model.
Create architecture and deployment diagrams.
Scaffold the TypeScript application with formatting, linting, validation, and test tooling.
Create reusable UI components, layouts, error boundaries, and accessibility conventions.
Implement environment configuration with startup validation.
Integrate customer identity and implement route protection.
Build dashboard, profile, and support-request workflows.
Implement database migrations, authorization checks, audit events, and safe error handling.
Add administrator capabilities only after the role model is approved.
Add unit, integration, and end-to-end tests.
Run dependency, secret, and static-analysis scans.
Test accessibility, responsive behavior, authentication boundaries, and failure states.
Define performance baselines and perform targeted load tests.
Create the repository under the approved GitHub owner.
Push the reviewed initial codebase using a protected default branch.
Configure pull-request reviews, status checks, Dependabot, code ownership, issue templates, and environment protections.
Document local setup, architecture, release, rollback, and incident procedures.
Define resource groups, App Service, PostgreSQL, Key Vault, Application Insights, Log Analytics, managed identities, and networking in Bicep.
Create separate development, staging, and production parameter files as required.
Apply least-privilege role assignments and configure secret references.
Configure database backups, retention, health checks, alerts, and budget notifications.
Configure GitHub Actions to authenticate to Azure using OpenID Connect rather than long-lived credentials.
Build, test, scan, package, provision, migrate, and deploy through staged jobs.
Deploy to a staging slot, run smoke tests, and swap to production after approval.
Retain the prior deployable artifact and define automated or manual rollback conditions.
Capture the failing workflow run, exact step, timestamps, commit SHA, deployment operation ID, and sanitized error output.
Check GitHub Actions logs, Azure Activity Log, App Service deployment logs, application logs, Application Insights traces, resource health, and database migration output.
Classify the failure as build, test, authentication, authorization, infrastructure, configuration, networking, migration, startup, health-check, quota, or runtime related.
Reproduce the narrowest failing operation in a non-production environment.
Form and test a root-cause hypothesis using logs and configuration evidence.
Correct the defect in source code, infrastructure code, permissions, configuration, or pipeline logic without bypassing security controls.
Rerun automated checks, redeploy to staging, execute smoke tests, and only then promote to production.
Document the root cause, impact, resolution, and preventive action; add a regression test or pipeline guard where feasible.

identityAndPermissions: Missing managed-identity access to Key Vault or database
networking: Private endpoint or DNS resolution issue
